description.narrative:
Rädda Barnen Norge har ansökt om stöd i syfte att genomföra programmet "Support for education and successful transitions among vulnerable children in South Sudan" under perioden 2019-2022.
Insatsen syftar till att erbjuda Sydsudanesiska pojkar och flickor tillgång till säker och jämlik utbildning av hög kvalitet. Det kommer att åstadkommas genom: 1) en ökning av antalet funktionella klassrum och utbildningscentrum som kan erbjuda barn och unga fullständig primärutbildning; 2) stärka utbildningens kvalitet genom vidareutbildning av lärare i framför allt inkluderande pedagogik och andra aktiviteter för att skolan ska bli en trygg och säker plats för lärande; 3) åtgärder för att engagera lokala samhällen och inkludera samhällsinstitutioner i styrandet av skolan samt öka lokalsamhällens förståelse för skolan och vikt av utbildning.
I enlighet med Internationella Rädda Barnens organisation ingår Sida avtal med Rädda Barnen Norge som kommer att ha det övergripande finansiella och administrativa ansvaret för insatsen. Rädda Barnen Norge kommer att vidareförmedla 83.3 miljoner svenska kronor till Rädda Barnen Sydsudan, resterande medel behålls av Rädda Barnen Norge och används till kostnader som administration, programutveckling och personalkostnader för personal som inte är direkt involverade i programmet. Rädda Barnen Sydsudan ansvarar för implementeringen av programmet tillsammans med fyra lokala partners: University of Juba, Light for the World, Support for Peace and Education Development Program (SPEDP) och Organization for Peace, Relief and Development (OPRD). Rädda Barnen Sydsudan betalar fakturor för aktiviteter utförda av partners och hanterar vidareförmedling till partners.

Save the Children Norway has applied to Sida for funding to carry out the programme "Support for education and successful transitions among vulnerable children in South Sudan" in South Sudan during the period 2019-2022.
The intervention aims at providing continued access to protective, quality and equitable education services for South Sudanese boys and girls. This will be achieved through: 1) an increase in the number of suitable facilities offering children and young people upper-primary and non-formal education services; 2) enhanced quality and inclusiveness of teaching methods and school-based protection mechanisms; and 3) efforts to engage communities and institutions in school governance and quality education delivery.
In accordance with Save the Children International overall organizational structure Sida will sign the agreement with Save the Children Norway that will have the financial oversight and administrative responsibility for the programme. Save the Children Norway will forward 83.3 million SEK to Save the Children South Sudan, the remaining funds will be used for overhead costs such as methodological development, administrative costs and staff costs for people not directly involved in the programme. Save the Children South Sudan will be responsible for implementation of the programme together with four technical and frontline partners: University of Juba, Light for the World, Support for Peace and Education Development Program (SPEDP) och Organization for Peace, Relief and Development (OPRD). Save the Children South Sudan will pay invoices for activities organized by partners and be responsible for forwarding of funds to partners.

The project aims to provide "increased and continued access to protective, quality and equitable education services through formal and non-formal education streams" for South Sudanese girls and boys in Eastern Equatoria and Jonglei States.
There are three outcomes: 1) Improved access to and completion of education or skills-based opportunities for children and youth in crisis-affected communities, 2) Enabling learning environments are supported by quality teaching, inclusive methodologies and school-based protection mechanisms, 3) Enhanced community-based and institutional system efficiency in school governance and education.

The final narrative report states that the project managed to deliver and implement all the planned activities regardless of challenges observed during the period of implementation, for example the setback due to the closures of schools because of COVID-19 in South Sudan. Working closely with the Ministry of General Education and Instruction, national implementing and the technical partners, the project has successfully delivered within the time frame and achieved its three outcome areas with the required budget attaining notable and acceptable gains among the stakeholders and strived to provide continuous access to safe, protective, quality, equitable and inclusive education for boys, girls, youth, and children with disabilities.
The project has rehabilitated 22 Temporary Learning Spaces (TLS), constructed 26 new gender segregated Ventilated Improved Pit (VIP) latrines, constructed 48 hand washing points, drilled 12 boreholes and installed it with the hand pumps to support and upgrade access to completion of educations of girls and boys. The intervention has also improved access to safe, protective quality and inclusive learning environments for the vulnerable children and youth in crisis affected communities in Kapoeta and Magwi that enabled factors for successful completion of education and transition of children from lower to upper primary and post primary education. Hence, the project has transformed dilapidated schools into revitalized educational spaces, creating an environment conducive to learning.
The project has achieved a total of 13,169 learners enrolled in primary, Accelerated Learning Programs, and basic vocational and life skills courses. This included 6,269 girls and 6,900 boys, representing 88% of the total target reach of 15,000 (6,000 female; 9,000 male). Girls' successful enrollment has attributed to several factors: special support programs for young mothers, improved construction of gender-segregated latrines, availability of water sources in school compounds to facilitate personal hygiene during menstruation, and provision of hygiene kits.
The project has supported and strengthened the capacity of volunteer teachers who gained professional skills and knowledge in teaching and are now able to apply acquired skills and knowledge adequately in different child centered pedagogical context which was translated in improvement of children performance and transition to the next class after sitting their end of year examination and certificate of primary education (CPE) within the project period. Magwi county was ranked the best in East Equatoria state in the 2022/2023 South Sudan Certificate of primary education because of the dedication of the volunteer teachers who have better knowledge and skills in teaching due to the training supported by the project as the county for years had been lagging in terms of children performance in national examinations.
In addition, the project has prepared volunteer teachers to continuously update their knowledge and skills and be able to teach the current South Sudan curriculum in an inclusive and learner-centered approach which helped overcome barriers limiting learners attendance and class participation.
To ensure safety, child friendly mechanisms and services were available to children in schools, the project has established and supported 27 Child Help Desks in the 27 Sida supported schools that supported in receiving, documenting, and referring identified critical cases to relevant service providers through the existing child protection monitoring and report mechanism. This has aided child participation in reporting all sorts of abuses encountered in the community and within the school making the school safe for learning with awareness sessions conducted by the 133 (99 female, 34 male) Child Help Desk focal point teachers, parents and school managers trained on child protection concerns and conducted school and community awareness on early child marriages, school related gender-based violence and teenage pregnancy that negatively affect education of a child in schools and communities. A total of 143 (69G:74B) cases were identified, assessed, and documented by the Child Help Desk focal point teachers and referred to case workers for further case management.
According to SCI, there has been visible reduction of violence and abuse in and around schools due to the sensitization and awareness fully propagated and disseminated by stakeholders, including the children themselves.
The project cost extension has had a significant gender approach aimed to reach and engage adolescent girls and boys in comprehensive sexuality education across the 27 supported schools. Comprehensive sex education curriculum initiated during the cost extension has educated learners and made them understand their identity, approaches to healthy sexual development and able to make informed decisions about their relationships, behaviors, and academic future.
To avoid schoolgirls and boys dropping out of schools and become young parents, the project has supported learners in schools through career guidance and mentorship. 4,163 learners (2,768 girls; 1,395 boys) attended and participated. It was evidenced that the career guidance and mentorship support to the school learners who regularly attended the sessions has had potential educational and behavioral benefits and had better academic performance in each end of school term.
The intervention has improved school governance and local education system due to functional parents and teachers association (PTA) and school management committee (SMC) across all Sida supported schools in Magwi and greater Kapoeta county. The PTA and SMC members have taken full responsibilities of quarterly back-to-school mobilization campaigns by organizing parents meetings and engage local chiefs to passed local orders for parents to send children to schools. The PTA and SMC members have developed school improvement plans and lead in sensitizing communities to embrace SCI initiatives to young mothers education with good number of young mothers returned to learn. Also, the presence of active and functional PTA/SMC bodies in the schools has increased parental involvement in school activities and decision-making processes.
Through the Sida project, SCI has worked closely with the Government on review and finalization of the Inclusive Education Policy for South Sudan, which was launched in July 2021. The policy was disseminated in all the five counties. The National Inclusive Education Policy is in line with the UNCRC and works towards equal access to quality education for all children including creating a safe and inclusive learning environment where all children feel safe and are supported to thrive. Also, the new national primary competency-based curriculum has been designed to meet the needs of all children as outlined in the National Inclusive Education Policy.
Finally, the project team was able to maintain good relationships with the State/County/Payam Education authorities, the National Ministry of General Education and Instruction, the Ministry of Gender, Child Welfare and Social Development and ensured their continued support and involvement in the implementation of the project activities.
Hence, the project reported commendable achievement of results. The intervention strengthened the completion of primary education by offering upper levels and reducing the impact of incomplete primary education cycles, ensuring that boys, girls, and learners with disabilities complete their primary education up to upper primary (from primary one to primary eight) even amid conflict. Also, the project made education in the communities more attractive, despite the struggle of food insecurity. Volunteer teachers were present in schools and were supported with incentives and capacity building, increasing their motivation, and enabling them to provide quality education to the children.
By constructing gender segregated pit latrines, it greatly contributed to the retention of schoolgirls to remain in schools, improve class performance and reach the upper classes. Also, the availability of safe and clean water sources in the schools has assisted learners to concentrate in the classrooms, elevated their physical activity in the compound, and reduced the frequency of illness.
After multiple training conducted, teachers did not only improve teaching of academic skills, but more importantly, the nurtured of a positive teacher-learner relationship that led to increased cooperation and engagement of learners and reinforced learners self-esteem in the classroom, increased motivation to holistic learning and built a foundation for academic performance. Also, the involvement of Parents Teachers Associations/School Management Committees in the awareness and identification of young mothers and children with disabilities boosted enrollment in all the supported schools.
Therefore, Sida assesses that SCI's capacity to reach set goals has been satisfactory, especially given the extremely challenging conditions that prevailed in the areas where the project was implemented and the focus on the most vulnerable children that the project had throughout the project period.
